note: Build a four-column backbone targeting C3 and C4 blends, C5 blend, and C6 paraffin blend while leaving heavier components for later evaluation.
notebook: PLAN: Step 1 test a compact blend-oriented backbone: split C4-/C5+, then C3/C4, C5/C6+, and C6 paraffins/heavier. Step 2 add ethane rejection and heavy product splits only where profitable; tune stages/reflux/pressure based on costs and purity. Start moderate settings to learn purities and economics.

note: Reposition the backbone to make the valuable C5 and C6-paraffin blends directly, with sharper splits and less boil-up than the failed initial cuts.
notebook: PLAN: Switch to a three-column blend backbone: feed split C5-/C6+, then C4-/C5 mix, then C6 paraffin mix/heavier. Sell C5 and C6 paraffin blends first; add C4 mix only if margins justify it. Current first split was badly positioned and too boilup-heavy, so no products qualified. Use sharper split around N-pentane/2,2-dimethylbutane with lower reboil and higher reflux.

note: Reduce size and severity across the backbone to restore convergence while retaining the intended C5 and C6 blend cuts.
notebook: PLAN: Restore convergence on a three-column blend backbone: root C5-/C6+, tops C4-/C5 blend, bottoms C6-paraffin blend/heavier. Sell C5 and C6 blends, then assess C4 and heavier cuts. Step 1: use shorter, lower-reflux columns and greater feed pressure drop to obtain a valid baseline. The prior 55-stage root failed all initialisations; earlier four-column design was valid but lost $1.023M-equivalent reward. Avoid tall/high-duty settings in this expensive scenario.

note: Monetise the large C5 blend immediately, recover the C3 blend by removing ethane, and sharpen the C4 bottoms with more boil-up.
notebook: PLAN: Build a converged blend-oriented backbone, monetise the valuable C5 cut first, then add C3/C4 purification and finally C6/heavy products only where profitable. Step 2: split BT into a C5 blend and C6-rich bottoms; split ethane from TT to sell C3 blend; increase T boil-up to reduce propane in TB C4 blend. Root/B settings remain 40/3/2. Existing costs are high, so avoid further large columns unless revenue clearly exceeds cost. Current baseline reward -0.719 with no sales; BT contains about 695 mol/s C5 and could earn roughly $600M/yr as a blend.

note: Sharpen the C5 and C3 cuts and keep residual butane out of the C5 stream; these three changes target about $850M/yr of blend revenue.
notebook: PLAN: Build a converged blend-oriented backbone, monetise C5 first, then C3/C4, and add C6/heavy products only if profitable. Step 3: make the C5 and C3 blends meet 95% by sharper root, BT and TT splits. Current valid reward -0.498; TB sells C4 ($159.7M). BT boil-up 2 left 85% C5 in BTT and much pentane in BTB, so raise BT to 6 with reflux 4. TT bottoms are 84% C3, so use 40/6/4. Root boil-up 3 should keep butane out of C5. Root/B costs dominate ($285M); after achieving sales, reduce their severity/size.

note: Restructure into a direct blend sequence with clean boiling-point gaps at each cut, reserving a stronger column for the difficult C6 paraffin/naphthene split.
notebook: PLAN: Rebuild as a direct sequence: root C4-/C5+, T C3-/C4, TT deethaniser, B C5/C6+, BT C6-paraffin/heavies. Monetise four blends, then tune purity and cost. The prior indirect tree distributed C5 across both root outlets and made purification expensive. The new cut boundaries are wide except N-hexane/MCP at BT, which gets 60 stages and reflux 6. Expected sale value is about $2.0B/yr if all four blends meet 95%.

note: Push butane and propane into their intended light streams, and drive pentanes overhead at BT; this also changes the invalid BT operating point.
notebook: PLAN: Direct blend sequence: root C4-/C5+, T C3-/C4, TT deethaniser, B C5/C6+, then add BB C6-paraffin/C6-naphthene+heavies. Step 1 is to restore a valid BT simulation while pushing residual butane overhead at the root and residual propane overhead at T. BT boil-up rises from 4 to 8 because its current bottoms retained roughly 230 mol/s N-pentane. C3 blend already earns $55.8M/yr. Target revenues are about C3 $56M, C4 $145M, C5 $618M and C6 paraffin $1.1B/yr. Avoid extra light-product columns: ethane and pure cuts are not economic here.

note: Concentrate on the two high-value blends: retain pentanes in the root bottoms, take a C5 cut at B, and split C6 paraffins from naphthenes and heavies at BTB.
notebook:
PLAN: Prioritise the two valuable cuts, C5 blend and C6-paraffin blend. Strip the uneconomic light-end subtree; root retains C5+ in B, B takes C5 overhead, and new BTB separates C6 paraffins overhead from naphthenes/heavies. Then tune for 95% blend purity and positive reward.
Current five-column design earns nothing and costs $495M/yr. Root boil-up 4 sends about 430 mol/s C5 overhead; reduce to 2 and raise reflux/stages. B boil-up 8 drives pentanes overhead. BTB currently has 82% C6 paraffin with 17% naphthenes, so a further split should unlock roughly $1.1B/yr. Do not pursue low-value C3/C4 until these cuts sell.

note: Revert to the best valid backbone; the current tree has no revenue and much higher cost.
notebook:
PLAN: Recover the best three-column blend backbone, inspect its exact stream compositions and costs, then make only targeted changes that create saleable C5/C6 or C3/C4 products without oversized columns. Stop if blend revenue cannot exceed energy/capital cost.
Current four-column configuration is unproductive ($750M/yr cost, no revenue). Reverting to turn-4 best (-0.498) to avoid compounding arbitrary tuning. Main lessons: very high boil-up is costly and can move desired components the wrong way; C6 paraffin cut is close to blend spec but current sequence is too expensive.

note: Test a lean two-column C5 blend train: remove C4 and lighter at the root, then take pentanes overhead from the bottoms.
notebook:
PLAN: Rebuild only the two-column C5 blend train with much lighter duties than earlier attempts; if C5 sells, optimise stage counts and reflux downward for positive net reward, otherwise try a single-column side draw.
C5 blend is worth about $611M/yr and is the cheapest valuable cut: root removes C4 and lighter across a wide boiling gap, B removes C6+ across the pentane/dimethylbutane gap. Avoid the unsuccessful C3 recovery and expensive C6 train. Current settings are deliberately moderate (40/2/2 then 50/3/3) to test whether two columns can beat their cost.
